after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨a,\,(3+2\text{i})b+c⟩$ if  

$\,$ $⟨b,a⟩=2\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨c,a⟩=1+\text{i}.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is antilinear in the second argument:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨a,\,(3+2\text{i})b+c⟩ & =⟨a,(3+2\text{i})b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ \\  & =(\overset{―}{3+2\text{i}})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ \\  & =(3-2\text{i})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-2\text{i})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ & =(3-2\text{i})\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}+\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨b,a⟩$ and $⟨c,a⟩:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-2\text{i})\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}+\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩} & =(3-2\text{i})\cdot \overset{―}{2\text{i}}+\overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\  & =(3-2\text{i})\cdot (-2\text{i})+(1-\text{i}) \\  & =-6\text{i}+4{\text{i}}^{2}+1-\text{i} \\  & =-6\text{i}+4(-1)+1-\text{i} \\  & =-3-7\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

    ⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ and ⟨a,αb⟩=α―⟨a,b⟩.

  • It has conjugate symmetry. For any a,b∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,b⟩=⟨b,a⟩―.

  • It is positive-definite. For any a∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,a⟩ is a non-negative real number, and ⟨a,a⟩=0 if and only if a=0.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨a,\,(4-\text{i})b+c⟩$ if  

$\,$ $⟨b,a⟩=-1-\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨a,c⟩=5.$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is antilinear in the second argument:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨a,\,(4-\text{i})b+c⟩ & =⟨a,(4-\text{i})b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ \\  & =(\overset{―}{4-\text{i}})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ \\  & =(4+\text{i})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4+\text{i})⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c\text{ }⟩ & =(4+\text{i})\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}+⟨a,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨b,a⟩$ and $⟨a,c⟩:$  

$$
\begin{aligned}(4+\text{i})\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}+⟨a,c⟩ & =(4+\text{i})\cdot (\overset{―}{-1-\text{i}})+5 \\  & =(4+\text{i})\cdot (-1+\text{i})+5 \\  & =-5+3\text{i}+5 \\  & =3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
